newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Rebel leader's son is new master of Kisangani.
newsitem.headline: Rebel leader's son is new master of Kisangani.

text.p: The 25-year-old son of Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila is in command in Kisangani, the key city captured by the rebels over the weekend.

In an interview with Reuters on Sunday, 25-year-old Joseph Kabila gave his title as "operational commander of the northern sector" for the rebel Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL).
"If I say people were excited it's an understatement," Kabila said of the warm welcome the rebels received when they entered Kisangani on Saturday after government troops fled.

Wearing a well-pressed uniform, Kabila looked like a soldier. Stocky like his father, a veteran opponent of Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko, Kabila spoke excellent English and chose his words with care.
Asked if he took orders from his father, based at the rebel capital in Goma, Joseph replied: "I take orders from the high command."
He said the rebels' biggest problem was a carpet of mines laid by government troops and their mercenary allies around every road into Kisangani apart from the one they used to retreat.
Kabila said demining was his priority because villagers were being killed by mines when they walked to their farms.
He put rebel casualties at only two and said 260 government soldiers had surrendered.
He said the real battle for Kisangani was on Monday and Tuesday last week about 20 kms (12 miles) east of the city.
"That was where we encountered real resistance. It lasted four days and we finally broke through their line on Friday. Then they scattered into the bush," he said.
The rebels secured the international airport at Kisangani at about 4 a.m. (0200 GMT) on Saturday.
"We found they had blown up the building they used as a command headquarters at the airport, the armoury and nearly all the artillery pieces," Kabila said.

But he denied reports the fleeing troops and mercenaries blew up their few airplanes and helicopters. The rebels found no aircraft at the airport and presumed the mercenaries, whom Kabila said were mainly French and ex-Yugoslavs, used them to fly out.
Kabila also dismissed reports that government troops attacked the mercenaries just before Kisangani's fall. He said they found no dead mercenaries at the airport or in town.
Asked when the fighting in Zaire would end, Kabila said: "The end of the war should be the end of the dictatorship."
